proved_step:
statement: Let G be a connected graph, c: V -> {0,1} with sum_v c(v) odd, and Tseitin(G,c) the GF(2) CNF on edge variables that contains, for each vertex v, every clause excluding one parity-violating assignment of the edges at v. Then every resolution refutation of Tseitin(G,c) contains a clause of width >= min{deg(v) : c(v) = 1}. Corollary: for K_n with c(0)=1 and c(v)=0 otherwise (n odd-sum parity fixed), every refutation has width >= n-1, so refutation width is unbounded in n for this encoding.
derivation: Let x = 0. For a vertex v with c(v)=0, the parity of x at v is even, so no clause of v's parity-violating family is falsified by x: every such clause is satisfied by x. For a vertex v with c(v)=1 and deg(v)=d, x has even parity at v, so the single clause of v's family that excludes x|_{edges at v} is falsified by x; that clause has width d. Let w < min{deg(v): c(v)=1}. Then every initial clause of width <= w is satisfied by x (clauses of charge-0 vertices by the parity argument, and charge-1 clauses have width >= min deg > w so they are absent). Resolution is sound: if C and D are satisfied by a fixed assignment x, every resolvent of C and D is satisfied by x. Hence every clause derivable with width <= w is satisfied by x, and the empty clause, which x does not satisfy, is not derivable. So no refutation of width <= w exists, i.e. every refutation has a clause of width >= min odd-charge degree. Check on bowtie (deg 4 at vertex 0): width >= 4 (matches measured minimal width 4 in cm-5e55529b375c468f, so tw+1 = 3 is refuted for this encoding). K_n with one odd vertex: width >= n-1 (measured K4: 4 >= 3; K5: >= 7 >= 4, so the bound is not tight there).
scope: Gf(2) Tseitin CNF with edge variables and all parity-violating clauses per vertex, as stated. Does not cover the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08 or any other encoding. Lower bound only; no upper bound claimed.

statement: Let F be an unsatisfiable CNF over Boolean variables and let x be any assignment. Let m(x) = min{|C| : C in F and x falsifies C} (m(x) = infinity if x falsifies no clause). Then every resolution refutation of F contains a clause of width >= m(x). Corollary: if some x falsifies only clauses of width >= m, then F has no refutation of width < m. The degree lemma S0003 is the special case F = Tseitin(G,c), x = 0.
derivation: Let P be a resolution refutation of F and suppose every clause of P has width < m(x). Each initial clause of P is a clause of F with width < m(x), so by definition of m(x) x satisfies it. Resolution is sound for a fixed assignment: if clauses C and D are both satisfied by x, a resolvent of C and D is satisfied by x, because the resolved variable is satisfied by x via one of C or D. By induction every clause of P is satisfied by x. The last clause of P is the empty clause, which x does not satisfy. Contradiction. Hence P contains a clause of width >= m(x). The corollary follows by taking x that falsifies only clauses of width >= m. Check: for x = 0 and Tseitin(G,c) with c(v)=1 at vertex v, m(0) = min odd-charge degree, which recovers S0003.
scope: Any unsatisfiable CNF F and any assignment x, resolution (Boolean, no weakening, width = max clause size in the refutation). Gives only a lower bound; it does not give an upper bound. It does not by itself say anything about the GF(3) kernel encoding of F(K_n) or about Search-MCSP. Its use for part (A) requires exhibiting, for a given CNF encoding of F(K_n), an x whose falsified clauses are all wide; that check is not done here.
